cues: Copper is a soft, reddish metal, second only to silver as a conductor.
In moist air it slowly grows a green patina of basic carbonate.
Heated in air it forms black copper two oxide, and above thirteen seventy kelvin, red copper one oxide.
Being below hydrogen, it does not react with dilute hydrochloric or sulphuric acid.
But oxidising acids attack it: hot concentrated sulphuric acid gives sulphur dioxide, dilute nitric acid gives nitric oxide, and concentrated nitric acid gives brown nitrogen dioxide.
text: Copper is a soft, reddish metal, second only to silver as a conductor. In moist air it slowly grows a green patina of basic carbonate. Heated in air it forms black copper two oxide, and above thirteen seventy kelvin, red copper one oxide. Being below hydrogen, it does not react with dilute hydrochloric or sulphuric acid. But oxidising acids attack it: hot concentrated sulphuric acid gives sulphur dioxide, dilute nitric acid gives nitric oxide, and concentrated nitric acid gives brown nitrogen dioxide.
